When I first started Dota 2, I went through all of Purge's newbie guide (it was recently revamped and and looks a lot better). The first bit goes over the very, very basics of the game which you're clearly familiar with at this point, but the majority of the rest of the guide contains a wealth of information that can help you improve.

This includes some recommended heroes to try out. Ideally, you should work towards knowing at least generally the strengths, weaknesses, and abilities of each of Dota's ~110 heroes, but if you're looking to branch out from the 3 you've listed, you can refer to that guide. Tinker is actually one of the more difficult heroes to play since he is quite vulnerable in lane, ideally gets jungle stacks (usually provided by supports), and necessitates good game sense and map awareness to understand where in the map you can and can't be (or should/shouldn't be) at any given time. Zeus and Omniknight are pretty great, though.

To answer your questions, I'm not sure what the maximum achievable MMR after your placement matches are, but anecdotally I think it's somewhere around ~4250 plus/minus a few hundred.

In terms of combos, Zeus has a lot of combo potential with other heroes that have global presence. One of the strongest is with Bloodseeker, as your ult will drop every enemy hero's HP down a significant percentage which enables Bloodseeker's passive, Thirst. Other heroes include Nature's Prophet (for ult and global TP), Ancient Apparition, and Spectre.
Tinker doesn't really combo with anyone that comes to mind since he's usually just a split pusher hanging out alone in the trees. There are a lot of different ways you can build Tinker item-wise, with the highest burst being something along the lines of Dagon 1 --> Eblade --> Dagon 5 --> Sheep/whaever (although they nerfed Dagon and Eblade a while back). Bloodstone, Sheep, Shiva's, and maybe even Eul's are all possible items you can build depending on the situation.
Sometimes I feel like Omniknights usefulness in a game is dependent more on the enemy team composition than your own. He easily wins teamfights if you're up against heroes that basically ONLY do damage with their right-clicks. PA, Lifestealer, Ursa, and Slardar, for example, simply can't do any significant amount of damage when Omni's ult is up. That said, Omni works best with melee carries such as PA, but also with heroes that naturally want magic immunity, such as Storm Spirit.
